_about: Field terms for F362, same shape as papers/glossary.json.

standard-uncertainty.field: metrology (the standard uncertainty of the GUM) and physics data tables
standard-uncertainty.definition: the plus-or-minus a table prints beside a value, meant as one standard deviation of the value's error; for a normal error the interval of one sigma either side holds the truth 68.27 percent of the time and two sigma 95.45 percent
standard-uncertainty.excludes: an expanded uncertainty already multiplied by a coverage factor, and any bound meant to hold always

coverage.definition: the share of cases in which an interval drawn round an earlier value contains the value that later replaced it; here the interval is one or two of the earlier value's own stated sigma either side
coverage.excludes: the share of intervals that contain the true value, which no later table can supply

shift-z.term: shift in units of the earlier sigma
shift-z.field: statistics, our usage; called a normalised residual in metrology
shift-z.definition: the size of the change in a quantity's value between an earlier and a later edition of a table, divided by the uncertainty stated in the earlier edition
shift-z.excludes: the sign of the change, and any uncertainty in the later value

needed-multiple.field: metrology, our usage; a coverage factor fitted after the fact
needed-multiple.definition: the multiple of the stated sigma that would have covered 68.27 or 95.45 percent of the later values; it is the matching percentile of the shifts in units of the earlier sigma, written k68 and k95
needed-multiple.excludes: a factor known before the later values were published

student-t.term: Student t distribution and its tail index nu
student-t.definition: a bell-shaped family with heavier tails than the normal curve; its degrees of freedom nu set the tail weight, so small nu means large shifts are common, nu of 1 is the Cauchy distribution and nu without limit is the normal curve

cauchy.definition: the Student t distribution with nu equal to 1, whose tails are so heavy that its mean and variance do not exist
cauchy.excludes: any distribution with a finite variance

moved-arm.definition: the same coverage count repeated after dropping every quantity whose value did not change between the two editions, since an unchanged value counts as covered whatever its stated uncertainty
moved-arm.excludes: a test of whether the unchanged values were right

proxy-truth.definition: a value fixed in advance and used in place of the unknown true value where no later edition settles it; here three values of the Hubble constant, 67.4, 70 and 73 km/s/Mpc, each reported on its own
proxy-truth.excludes: a claim that any of the three is the true value

shared-inputs.definition: measurements or derived values that feed both an earlier and a later edition of a table, so that the two editions are not independent and agree more than independent work would
shared-inputs.excludes: measurements made only for the later edition

bootstrap.definition: redrawing the quantities of a table with replacement, here 300 times, and recomputing the coverage each time; the middle 95 percent of the recomputed values is the interval
bootstrap.excludes: uncertainty from the choice of editions or from shared inputs, which resampling quantities does not touch

honest-gaussian.definition: simulated shifts drawn from a standard normal distribution at the PDG sample size, so that every stated sigma is exactly right, scored the same way as the real shifts
